stickers: Not your fault. Let's fix it 💛

figures.alt: The mastitis spectrum from mild to serious: narrowed duct, inflammatory mastitis, bacterial mastitis, and abscess.
figures.caption: Mastitis is a spectrum. Most cases stay on the left side of it.

figures.alt: Swelling loop: tissue swells, ducts narrow, milk slows, pressure builds, more swelling. Calming the swelling breaks the loop.
figures.caption: Calm the swelling and the loop starts to break.

figures.alt: Two columns. In the breast: warm, tender wedge, red or darker skin, firm area, pain while feeding. In the body: fever 100.4 or higher, chills, aches, wiped out.
figures.caption: One sore spot plus flu-like aches is the classic pair.

figures.alt: Comparison: engorgement affects both sides early on; narrowed duct is a tender lump without fever; mastitis is a hot red wedge with fever; abscess is a lump that stays or grows and needs an ultrasound.
figures.caption: Quick sort for a sore breast while feeding.

figures.alt: Two columns. Helps: feed on demand, cold packs, feather-light strokes toward the armpit, supportive bra, rest. Skip: deep massage, long heat, extra pumping, stopping feeds suddenly.
figures.caption: Gentle care that calms swelling. General education, not a personal plan.

stickers: The ER beats a text here

figures.alt: Red warning list: fever 103 or higher, spreading red streaks, pus or a growing lump, shaking chills, racing heart, faint or confused. Go to the ER or call 911.
figures.caption: Any of these? Skip the text. Go to the ER or call 911.

figures.alt: Feeding tips: start on the comfortable side, point the baby's chin toward the sore spot, feed on demand, no extra pumping, hand express just for comfort.
figures.caption: Small changes that make feeding easier while you heal.

figures.alt: Two doors. Text visit: one sore red area, fever under 103, eating and drinking, no pus or lump. In person or ER: any red flag, a growing lump, not better after 48 hours, not breastfeeding.
figures.caption: Where your story fits. When in doubt, go in.
